_notes: Spider-Man Vault Edition (V1.01) - Stern SAM platform.
Published map: https://github.com/tomlogic/pinmame-nvram-maps (maps/stern/sam/smanve_101.map.json).
CONFIRMED against a genuine real capture from the office cabinet (2026-08-17, provided by Magnus):
slot 0 (0x2b80) = 'SSR'/150000000 (untouched factory demo score),
slot 1 (0x2ba0) = 'RAT'/130296090 (matches Magnus's reported 130,296,088 to within 2 - likely a display
misread of the last two digits, not a format error),
slot 3 (0x2be0) = 'LFS'/120000000, slot 4 (0x2c00) = 'RAT'/107481350 - all real player data, not synthetic.
This is the strongest evidence yet that the Stern SAM high-score layout (11-byte null-terminated ASCII
initials + 4-byte little-endian int score, 0x20 stride, no checksum) is correct for genuine hardware,
not just internally-consistent sample data. See xmn_151h.map.json for the still-unverified X-Men case.
CONFIDENCE: high (independently published AND matches real captured data byte-for-byte on 4 of 5 fields
checked, with the 5th off by a plausible transcription typo).
CRITICAL CORRECTION (2026-08-17): the 2 bytes immediately after each score/counter field are NOT fixed
0xFF padding as originally documented here and by tomlogic - they're a 2-byte tag/checksum that is a
function of that record's (initials, score) content and travels WITH the record when the leaderboard
re-sorts it to a different rank/address (confirmed: the real 'LFS'/120000000 entry has the exact same
tag bytes whether it's stored at the Third Place address or, in the factory-default file, the First
Place address). Only the 2 bytes after THAT (before the next slot) are genuinely fixed 0xFF.
This tag is almost certainly the actual write-protection mechanism: writing a new score/initials without
recomputing the matching tag causes the whole record (not the whole block) to be rejected on boot and
replaced with the ROM's compiled-in factory default for that slot - confirmed via a live isolated test
(only 'Spider Champion' edited, tag left stale -> only that record reverted, others untouched).
Exact algorithm NOT yet cracked - quick attempts (8/16-bit sum inverted per the general checksum8/16
convention, CRC16-CCITT, CRC16-IBM, over several candidate byte spans) did not reproduce the known
tag values. Could be a different checksum entirely, or not content-derived at all (e.g. a write-sequence
nonce used to arbitrate between a primary/shadow copy). See project_competition_mode_design memory for
the full real (initials, score, tag) dataset used to test this.
CRACKED (2026-08-17): disassembled the actual game ROM (smanve_101.bin, provided by Magnus) and found
the checksum routine directly. tag = 0xFFFF - (sum of the 28 bytes from record start through the end
of the score field, as plain unsigned bytes, mod 65536), stored as the 2-byte tag at record+0x1c.
Confirmed by computing it for all 24 known real/factory-default records collected so far: 24/24 matched
exactly. This is almost certainly why every prior write test failed - we never recomputed this tag, so
every edited record failed the ROM's own boot-time validation and got replaced with the compiled-in
default for that slot. research/patch_nvram_score.py now computes and writes this automatically.
Also corrected 'Best Combo Champion' below: the originally-copied tomlogic map claimed a 1-byte counter
at +0x1a, which cannot hold LEE's real value (327681) and is contradicted by the checksum match using
the standard 4-byte-at-+0x18 layout - fixed to match what's actually confirmed correct.
